clue.text: Radio set destroyed in sun orbiter

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wireless set smashed to pieces somewhere in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are small rocky bodies circling the sun, mostly in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.

clue.text: Allotting term to an overthrown imperial dynasty

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, so the little word before it is flipped round

blocks.note: taken as written
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: Assigning a word to some toppled royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming something is giving it a word or label, assigning it what it will be called.

clue.text: 24 hours doubled up and so on?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: twenty-four hours is a day, and doubled means written twice

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum: a whole day, twice over, and then some.
explanation.walkthrough: A DAY written twice gives ADAYADAY, which read upwards spells YADA YADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yada yada is a slangy dismissal meaning blah blah, standing for tedious further talk not worth repeating.

clue.text: Stunning swimmer's thrilling fact needing correction somewhat?

indicators.note: a statement needing correction must be put right, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an electric atmosphere is a thrilling one
the four letters to be rearranged
the suffix -ish means somewhat, as in greenish

explanation.surface: A fish's amazing fact turns out to be a little bit wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunning' looks like praise but is literal: this fish delivers an electric shock to stun prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric catfish of African rivers can discharge several hundred volts, stunning prey and predators alike.

clue.text: Two red berries for William Joyce?

blocks.note: haws are the red berries of the hawthorn, and there are two of them

explanation.surface: A pair of red berries offered to a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: William Joyce broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain in the Second World War and was nicknamed Lord Haw-Haw for his drawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Haw-Haw was the nickname given to the wartime propaganda broadcaster, hanged for treason in 1946.

clue.text: Old English walls cold in one church

definitions.note: describes someone belonging to one particular church

indicators.note: walls surround what lies inside, so the old dialect goes round the next piece

blocks.note: Anglian was a dialect of Old English spoken by the Angles
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An old English building whose walls keep the cold inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglican means belonging to the Church of England or its sister churches in the worldwide communion.

clue.text: Waters that had a big part in Exodus?

definitions.text: Waters that had a big part in Exodus?

blocks.clueFragment: had a big part in Exodus
blocks.note: surface reading: an actor who landed a major role in a film or biblical drama
setter's reading: waters that were parted wide, as Moses divided them for the Israelites to cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a big part' sounds like a starring role; it means was split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Exodus the waters are divided so the Israelites can escape Egypt on dry ground.

clue.text: Main restriction almost absent in trade

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in places the shortened word inside the next one

blocks.note: to trade goods is to sell them
someone absent is away

explanation.surface: A trade barrier that is very nearly missing from commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, so a main restriction is a barrier that keeps the sea out; it is not about trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea wall is a barrier built along a coast to hold back the ocean, the main in poetic language.

clue.text: Orphaned character pawning item here and there

indicators.note: here and there suggests taking letters at intervals, every other one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An orphan forced to pawn belongings in scattered places.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical heroine raised in an orphanage.

clue.text: Patriarch against wearing Hawaiian garland

indicators.note: something wearing a garland has it around it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower necklace
V is short for versus

explanation.surface: An old patriarch protesting while wearing a flower necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob and the forefather of one of the twelve tribes of Israel, the priestly Levites.

clue.text: In which one's local confused with home endlessly?

definitions.text: In which one's local confused with home endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means with the last letter cut off
confused means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: one is I, plus the S of the possessive
taken as written
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A condition in which someone confuses the pub with home.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British neighbourhood pub; the whole clue also describes the answer, where the pub becomes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Addiction to drink could be described as a state where a person treats the neighbourhood pub as their house.

clue.text: Hippie look no good with hard expression

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
NG is the abbreviation for no good
H is hard, as on pencils
an air is a manner or look on someone's face

explanation.surface: A hippie's appearance dismissed as no good, with a stern face.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhair is dated slang for a hippie or counterculture type with uncut hair.

clue.text: With John Adair say inspired by cool principle used around here?

indicators.note: breathed in by, so the pair of names goes inside the word for cool
say flags that the surname stands for a nickname by example

blocks.note: W is short for with
to ice something is to cool it
john and can are both slang for a toilet
Red Adair was the famous oil-well firefighter

explanation.surface: A management guru's cool rule applied in this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: John Adair suggests a single person, a leadership writer; it splits into John and Adair. 'Around here' hints at a coven's own ethic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wiccan Rede is the core ethical maxim of modern witchcraft: harm none and do as you will.

clue.text: Regularly find clues not working

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A solver regularly finds the clues aren't working.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes a person or machine doing nothing, out of action or unemployed.

clue.text: Able to stimulate old worker around City dumping yen

indicators.note: dumping means throwing away, so the named letter leaves
around means the first pieces enclose the next

blocks.note: ex means former
taken as written before trimming
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A former employee in the City who has offloaded his yen.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, which makes yen-dumping sound like currency trading.
explanation.definitionFit: An excitant is a stimulant; as an adjective it means tending to arouse or excite activity.

clue.text: Caught twice breaking into a house in Acre once

indicators.note: a burglar breaking into a building ends up inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
C is caught in cricket scoring, written twice
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A burglar caught twice breaking into the same house.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre is the ancient port in northern Israel, not a unit of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Accho is the old biblical name for the port city now called Acre or Akko.

clue.text: How to obtain funds unduly from extra lottery?

blocks.note: over means additional, left over
a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: A tip on getting extra money from a lottery win.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw an account is to withdraw more money than it holds.

clue.text: Drink nothing? Impossible!

blocks.note: nog is a drink, as in eggnog
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone refusing a drink outright.
explanation.definitionFit: No-go means not possible or ruled out, as in a no-go area.

clue.text: Superb commercial inspiring daughter's older relative

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the pair takes the next piece inside

blocks.note: grand means splendid
D is short for daughter
a TV commercial is an ad

explanation.surface: A fine advertisement that motivates a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A granddad is a grandfather, a relative two generations older than oneself.

clue.text: Zoom lens?

blocks.note: surface reading: a camera lens of variable focal length
setter's reading: the video-calling app, so the lens is the little camera used for online calls

explanation.walkthrough: Zoom is capitalised because it is the video-call service, not the photographic zoom.
explanation.definitionFit: The small computer camera used for video meetings over the internet is the eye that Zoom calls rely on.

clue.text: Unfinished base in Fenland city in a bad way?

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is missing
in puts the trimmed word inside the place name

blocks.note: Ely is the cathedral city in the Cambridgeshire Fens
base means low and vile

explanation.surface: An incomplete military base in a fenland cathedral city, run badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun for a camp, but it is the adjective meaning morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: Evilly is an adverb meaning wickedly, acting with malice.

clue.text: Jellyfish in sea to America's north?

indicators.note: in a down answer, north of means placed above, so earlier

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the United States

explanation.surface: A jellyfish swimming in the sea off America's northern coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A medusa is the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish, named for the snake-haired Gorgon.

clue.text: Beer served with tuna one ordered in these islands?

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged differently, putting letters into a new sequence

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
tuna plus one as I

explanation.surface: A beer and a tuna dish ordered on some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aleutian Islands form a long chain stretching west from Alaska across the northern Pacific.

clue.text: Set about Pole tucking into rotten trout

indicators.note: rotten food has gone off and fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged
tucking into means going inside, eating into something

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A man from Poland tucking into a rotten fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish man; it is a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to a task is to set about it, beginning work with energy.

clue.text: Arts festival: see it anew, following round in 3D?

indicators.note: anew means made over again, so these letters are freshly arranged
in places the pair inside the three letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
three Ds
F is short for following
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An arts festival urging you to watch again, after a round in 3D.
explanation.walkthrough: 3D is read as three letter Ds, not three-dimensional.
explanation.definitionFit: An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music, poetry and literature with competitions.

clue.text: See 13
Start to license tattoos for associates

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
to ink someone is to tattoo them

explanation.surface: Getting a licence to do tattoos for colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are connections or ties, and to link things is to associate them.

clue.text: Letters from Kish as transcribed for sacred writing

indicators.note: letters from means a run of consecutive letters taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Letters from the ancient city of Kish copied out as scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Kish was an ancient city of Sumer, which makes the surface about cuneiform letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shastra is a Hindu treatise or scripture, a text of sacred instruction.
